patients.summary: Administrative assistant with long-standing SLE on hydroxychloroquine and prednisone, hypertension, steroid-related AVN of the right hip and osteopenia, who joined in 2020. documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
44F, administrative assistant, transferring care; wanted a practice where she can reach her doctor directly given how much specialty care she has.

HPI: Lupus since ~2011, sees outside rheumatology twice a year. Joints "mostly behaving," some tiredness most days. On hydroxychloroquine and prednisone 10 for years, never got below that without trouble. BP checked at home occasionally, usually high 130s. Right hip aches with long walks; had core decompression 2019, uses no aid.

PMH: SLE. HTN. AVN R femoral head s/p core decompression 2019. Osteopenia (DXA 2019).
PSH: R hip core decompression 2019.
Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 bid, prednisone 10 qd, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25, vit D3 2000 u, calcium carbonate 600 bid. Tylenol now and then.
Allergies: sulfonamides - severe rash.
FH: mother SLE. Father HTN, T2DM. Sister Hashimoto.
SH: married, lives in Holyoke. Office job. Never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs.

Exam: well-appearing, NAD. HEENT: oral mucosa moist, no ulcers. Neck supple, no lymphadenopathy, thyroid normal. CV RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT, spleen not palpable. Ext: no edema. Joints: no synovitis today. R hip: flexion mildly limited, internal rotation uncomfortable at end range. Skin: no rash.

A/P:
1. SLE on chronic prednisone - stable per patient; continue current regimen, rheum managing. Will get baseline CBC, CMP, UA.
2. HTN - above goal today, home readings similar. Continue 3-drug regimen, bring home log next visit.
3. AVN R hip - stable symptoms, activity as tolerated.
4. Osteopenia on long-term steroids - continue Ca/D, vit D level. DXA repeat in 2022.
5. HM: flu shot today. Hep C screen. Mammogram due 10/2020, ordered. Pap due 2021. Lipids, A1c.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Aisha, your labs from Monday look good. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, urine, sugar, cholesterol and vitamin D are all in an acceptable range, and the hepatitis C screen was negative. Potassium is on the low side of normal, which is common with HCTZ; we'll keep checking it. See you in December.

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO views with tomosynthesis. Comparison 10/2019. Breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses. No suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion. No change from prior.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice. Date of visit: 02/08/2021.

Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Diallo, 44, in follow-up for systemic lupus erythematosus.

Over the last several months she has felt persistently fatigued, with aching in many joints and occasional low-grade fevers. She also describes skin changes after sun exposure and mouth sores that keep coming back.

Current medications: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily, prednisone 10 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, cholecalciferol 2000 units, calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily. Apart from these she uses an over-the-counter pain reliever only occasionally.
Allergies: sulfonamides (severe rash).

On exam she looked tired but comfortable. There was faint erythema across the malar area. Both wrists had mild synovial fullness. I saw a few shallow ulcers on the buccal mucosa. Heart and lung exams were normal.

Labs today show a mild normocytic anemia and a positive ANA. Creatinine and urinalysis are normal, with no sign of renal involvement.

Assessment: SLE with ongoing constitutional, mucocutaneous and joint symptoms. Given more than a decade of continuous glucocorticoid exposure she should be regarded as immunosuppressed; I have added this to her problem list and would ask that she be vaccinated accordingly and that infections be evaluated with a low threshold.

Plan: continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily and prednisone 10 mg daily. I will see her again in the summer.

Rheumatology

conditions.label: Secondary hyperaldosteronism due to dietary sodium restriction

medications.drug: potassium chloride 20 MEQ Extended Release Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily with food

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Hypertension Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back for BP. Rheum saw her in Feb for fatigue and joint aches. Says she takes the amlodipine, lisinopril and HCTZ every day, pharmacy fill history agrees. No headache, chest pain or palpitations. Brought log: mostly 145-155/90s. Still following a very strict low-salt diet she started on her own years ago - no added salt, low-sodium everything.

O: BP 154/96, HR 78. Looks well hydrated. Lungs clear, heart regular. No edema.
Labs 5/4: Na 146, K 3.1, Cl 108, HCO3 32, Cr 0.9. Plasma renin activity 7.4 (high), aldosterone 26 (high).

A/P:
1. Hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis with high renin and high aldosterone on ACEi + thiazide in the setting of severe dietary sodium restriction -> secondary hyperaldosteronism. Pattern is not one of primary aldosteronism (renin is high, not suppressed).
 - Start KCl ER 20 mEq daily.
 - Ease off the extreme salt restriction to ordinary moderate intake (normal cooking, still avoid processed/very salty foods). Discussed at length; she was surprised.
 - BMP 2 wks.
2. HTN, not at goal on 3 drugs. Keep same doses for now, reassess after K corrected and diet adjusted.

RTC 3 months, sooner prn.

documents.title: Potassium recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Aisha - potassium is back to 4.0 and the bicarbonate came down to 27, so the supplement plus the diet change is working. Keep both going. Send me a few home BP readings in a month.

documents.title: RE: Potassium recheck
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thank you. Honestly it's nice to put a little salt back on my eggs.

documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice. Visit 07/30/2021.

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Diallo returns. The arthralgia and fatigue I described in February have not settled on her current regimen; she is struggling to get through work days.

I have increased prednisone from 10 mg to 20 mg daily and will try to come back down once she is more comfortable. Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily continues. She is aware of the bone and hip risks of the higher dose given her history of avascular necrosis.

Allergies: sulfonamides.

Follow-up here in 6 months.

Rheumatology

VA 20/20 OU. IOP normal. Anterior segment quiet. Dilated fundus exam: normal maculae, normal vessels and optic nerves OU. SD-OCT: intact ellipsoid zone, no parafoveal thinning OU. 10-2 visual fields: full OU.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Rheum bumped prednisone to 20 a few weeks ago; joints a bit better, sleeping a little worse, appetite up. On KCl daily, using salt normally now. Home BPs better, 130s/80s.

O: BP and HR as charted. Lungs clear. RRR. No edema. Walking without limp.

A/P:
1. HTN - improved since the diet change. Continue.
2. Secondary hyperaldosteronism / K - on KCl, BMP today.
3. SLE - prednisone 20 per rheum. CBC today, last Hgb mildly low at rheum in Feb.
4. Counseled on the steroid dose and her hip; call if hip pain worsens.

Physical next month.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45F annual.

Interval: prednisone up to 20 mg (rheum, 7/2021). Started KCl in May for low K. Feels OK, mild fatigue her usual. Hip occasional ache. Mood fine.

Meds: HCQ 200 bid, prednisone 20 qd, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25, KCl 20 mEq, D3 2000 u, Ca carbonate 600 bid.
Allergies: sulfa (severe rash).

ROS otherwise negative.
Exam: well. HEENT normal, no oral ulcers today. Neck no nodes, thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts symmetric, no masses, no axillary nodes. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vagina and cervix normal, Pap/HPV collected. Ext no edema. Skin: no rash.

PHQ-9: 3.

Plan:
- Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, UA.
- Pap/HPV done today.
- Flu shot + pneumococcal (PCV20, indicated given chronic steroid immunosuppression) at a nurse visit next month when available.
- Shingrix series this winter.
- Colon cancer screening now due at 45 - referral to GI for colonoscopy, she'd like to wait until spring.
- Mammogram 2022.
- Annual eye screening for HCQ done 8/2021.

RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your physical labs and Pap are all fine - kidney function, potassium, blood counts, cholesterol and sugar in range, urine clear, Pap and HPV negative. Nothing to change.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine. BP fine at home and here. Right hip has been bothering her more since around October, worse on stairs and at the end of the day; she thought it was the cold. No fall. Taking Tylenol.

Exam: BP as charted. Gait slightly antalgic on R. R hip IR painful and limited.

A/P: HTN controlled. K on KCl - BMP. R hip pain with known AVN on prednisone 20 - if not settling in a few weeks, imaging; she will call. Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months.
